title: Feature Highlights
desc: A scannable tour of Audiobook Studio's capabilities — voices and cloning, the queue and recovery, assembly and export, the plugin SDK, and the external API.
lede: A quick, scannable tour of what Audiobook Studio can do. Each capability has its own deeper page later in the handbook.
body:
At a glance
  • Voices, variants, and cloning, organized in a real library.
  • A reliable queue with progress and restart recovery.
  • Assembly and export to M4B / MP3.
  • Extensible: a plugin SDK and an external API.

Voices, variants & cloning

Build a voice once, reuse it everywhere. Create voices from audio samples, keep multiple variants, and identify them with icons and tags. Voices are independent of any one engine. See Voices and the Voice Lab.

Queue, progress & recovery

Long jobs are handled gracefully. Generation and assembly run through a queue with live progress and ETAs. If the app restarts, work recovers — completion is judged by validated audio artifacts, not by whether a file happens to exist.

Assembly & export

End up with a real audiobook. Combine finished chapters into an M4B (or MP3) you can keep, play on any device, and share — with editable metadata and chapter titles.

Extensibility

  • Plugin SDK. Wrap any TTS engine behind a small contract and publish it.
  • External API. Use Studio as a local text-to-speech backend for your own scripts.
Coming with 2.0 — installable engines from GitLab, a Hugging Face voice library, and AI voice casting. See Plugin SDK.

Where to go next

Ready to install? Head to Getting Started. Want the concepts first? Start with Core Concepts.
